HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Meta.Meta__Description: Timber grain - long, gently waving lines, unevenly spaced, running across the tile and joining the next. For a joist, a rafter or a plate drawn along its length.
HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Meta.Meta__WhyPaperUnits: Every length here is PAPER millimetres, like the dash patterns in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json, so the hatch measures the same on the sheet at 1:20 and at 1:100. Pattern scale adjusts from there.
HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Meta.Meta__WhySeams: Every line crosses the left and right seams travelling dead level, and none comes within 1.4 mm of the top or bottom edge. Na__LeHatch__SeamCopies paints what the next tile pushes across.
HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Meta.Meta__WhyUneven: Four lines at uneven heights with different waves. Evenly spaced identical waves read as corrugated sheet, not as wood.

HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Identity.Identity__Description: How this pattern is named, found and grouped in the pattern lists.
HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Identity.Identity__Note: Timber shown along its length. Turn it with Pattern deg to run with the member.

HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Tile.Tile__Description: The repeating cell, in paper millimetres.
HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Tile.Tile__Note: Long and shallow: grain runs a long way before it repeats.

HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Defaults.Defaults__Description: What the pattern draws with until a use sets its own. The stroke is 0.25 pt (0.0882 mm) at scale 1 and grows with the pattern scale; a line weight typed in the panel does not. 'inherit' takes the colour of whatever carries the hatch - a vector's edge colour - until a pattern colour is picked.

HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Glyphs.Glyphs__Description: Drawn about the glyph's own origin, y pointing DOWN, in tile millimetres. Strokes only: the PDF stamps a tile as lines and never fills one.

GrainA.Glyph__Note: The first and last control points share the height of the ends, so the line leaves one tile and enters the next dead level: no kink at the seam.

GrainB.Glyph__Note: Level at both ends, by the same rule.

GrainC.Glyph__Note: Level at both ends and at its middle.

HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Placements.Place__Note: A wider gap, then the busiest line
Bottom line, 1.5 mm clear of the edge

HatchPattern__TimberGrain__Bounds.Bounds__Description: How far a use may scale and turn this pattern before it stops reading as the material.
